I wouldn’t be writing this review, if I had been capable of talking to actual person! In the middle of the night, while I was asleep, someone succeeded at hacking into one of my Instagram accounts…after only two failed attempts! At the time of the first two attempts, which, again, happened while I was asleep, Instagram sent codes to my phone. On the third attempt, a message was sent to me via WhatsApp, informing me that my account had been accessed. That was just after 2AM. 

When I discovered these messages, after I woke up, at around 8AM, I clicked on a link that required me to verify whether it was me who had logged in. I, of course, clicked on “This wasn’t me.” Nothing happened! Every time I tried clicking on that option, a message popped up saying, “Something went wrong. Please try again.” It just said that over and over again. I was horrified. I had two Instagram accounts. The one that was hacked into, I simply deleted because I wasn’t using it that much anyway. 

The big problem is, the account that was hacked into was connected to my other, more important account, as well as my Facebook profile. I wonder what information the hacker stole! Lord knows, they had plenty of time to take whatever they wanted! The most I could do was chat with an AI bot about it! I gave this app two stars, instead of one, only because there is plenty about Instagram that I actually like, but what is it worth to have such a social media account when things like this can happen so easily?!
attributes.title: Questionable security and no human being to talk to about it!

The rectangular grid system is uprooting a fundamental element that made IG what it was. Remember back in the day when IG filters came with a SQUARE frame option? You’ve changed it back and forth several times, and of my two profiles, sometimes one of them has a square profile grid, and the other has rectangle, and that’s just from me toggling from one to the other in the same minute. I believe a rectangle display works as a fantastic method for displaying IG Reels, but I think we can all agree that squares are a foundational display method. attributes.review:
I’ve been on insta for quite a while, but I’ve noticed that some of the features (noticeably the ones that are also shared, or should I say dominated by other apps) need improvement.
1) Close friends stories. Why can I only have one? If the goal was to implement similar features to sn*pchat, then why can’t I have multiple close friends for different friend groups/family/business partners? It’s been years since this feature has been available on other apps and Meta has made no effort to improve upon it, opting instead for location mapping (which most don’t use due to larger following or public accounts) and Instagram notes (attention seeking).
2) Login/security. Why can I not connect my iCloud account to Meta and use it to log in? From anecdotes, many of my friends have had their instagrams hacked, but it seems like iCloud is generally harder for scammers to access…additionally, getting locked out of my Instagram accounts has happened to me more than once. Meta should consider implementing this feature like other social media apps have.
3) finally, the algorithm isn’t as good as other social media apps. Understandably some, including myself, may be concerned about the lack of privacy and the information Meta is obtaining. However, given how much information is already available to them upon making an account, I would expect higher quality content on reels and suggested posts than what I am currently seeing.
More than willing to adjust my review should I see these features implemented.
attributes.title: Algorithm, stories, and login/security need some work

A more egregious issue for me though is the fact that I can’t permanently mute “suggested” posts in my feed. Instagram’s recent security systems seem overly aggressive and opaque, leading to many legitimate users being unable to access their accounts for days with no clear explanation or resolution path. Reports from users across the U.S. indicate that thousands of people believe flaws in Meta’s automated security and moderation tools have led to false lockouts and account suspensions. According to a recent Boston 25 Now story, “thousands of Facebook and Instagram users believe a flaw in Meta’s security AI has led to false accusations and wrongful lockouts,” with users struggling to regain access and contact support effectively.  ￼

This problem is not isolated — widespread complaints, historic pressures from state attorneys general over takeovers and lockouts, and third-party reports about usability issues highlight systemic challenges. In fact, a 2024 letter from 40 state attorneys general to Meta called for “immediate action” to better prevent account takeovers and lockouts because consumer complaints had surged sharply.  ￼ Instagram and Meta need to improve their account recovery tools, transparency on how security decisions are made, and direct human support options so that users aren’t helpless when the automated systems mistakenly block them.

attributes.review: Instagram gives many options for making noises and sounds. To find a rudiment or a routine in which to practice that rudiment, can be foundational to growth in expression of that connective yearning we experience within the culture and further within the connective culture that is social media, and of which Instagram seeks to embody itself as the essential mode therein. Instagram like Facebook and Twitter (I imagine because I do not have a Twitter myself) amplifies a voice and diminishes what may be an understood or perhaps an un-understood emotion. The gambit is that the voice which resonates will be that of an emotion which is understood and thereby lead to resolution through unification via the platform. By being lent or given I suppose you could say an eye into another person’s world we are theoretically also offered an eye into his/her/their soul(s). What do we do with what is witnessed and do we have the wherewithal to do anything with it at all aside from witness, and should we if we do? Are all questions a person will experience in the medium. What’s perhaps the most destabilizing experience one can have is realizing that the app like any app or forum or place is real in the same way in that the interaction is genuine insofar as you the user believe it to be, the caveat being that you the user bring forth that which is already there during before and after the interaction, rendering the manipulative quality,I.e. the fake aspect, of the forum meaningless insofar as it is understood to be so. And meaningful insofar as it is understood to be meaningless. Loving insofar as it is understood to be empty. And comforting insofar as it is without human touch.

attributes.review: In the current climate, there are atrocities happening and social media was always a great way to shed light on crimes against humanity that would normally go on noticed. However, Instagram today has taken it upon themselves to silence and/or censor voices from people of oppression or from people that has suffered from said atrocities including genocide. These people include: press, influencers or victims, and/or political figures. It’s deeply saddening and frustrating to see that a viewpoint that is so clearly racist with hateful propaganda are left unaffected. Ironic how instagram will attempt to save face by claiming “everyone is entitled to their own opinion” yet silences someone’s opinion over the other’s. Clearly, Instagram lacks the moral competency to see how a page promoting violence against a certain ethnic group is much more harmful than a Instagram page covering current, sometimes graphic, events. Instagram has a lot of potential to be an outlet for social change—but instead peddles to the distractions, consumerism, and allows racism and xenophobia to flourish. Instagram is not a place where you have a voice or an opinion—you’re not even allowed to dislike anything. Imagine that dystopia.

I have been using instagram for almost 3 years, and have made my way into the fandom side of Instagram lately. I have a fan account that is in danger of being reported and taken down. Lately, many people across fandoms have had their accounts taken down from other users reporting their accounts for impersonating YouTubers or celebrities. Instagram had the chance to review the accounts and made the decision to take the accounts down. They did nothing wrong and were not impersonating anyone. One of the accounts even had the words “fan page” in their bio. You need to hire better people to review the reports, or have actual people review them and not robots.
I also don’t like how there are more ads on the site. And most of them are scams. I’ve seen some good ads for real businesses, but a lot of the ads I’ve seen are just random companies promoting random things that don’t interest me. Those are the ads that annoy me the most. I have to scroll very far down just to see the accounts I want to see, and not accounts Instagram thinks I want to see. I’m usually very active on certain accounts, but I still don’t see enough posts from them. I have to have notifications on to actually see all the posts. 
Instagram is a great app though, aside from them taking down accounts and random promotions. I love the new layout, and the explore page is better than it was a few years ago, in my opinion. I do like the communities it creates. 
But, as a final analysis, I think that Instagram should have a better review team, and should target ads better and less often.

attributes.review: I’ve been using the app instagram for as long as I can remember. I can say that it is a part of me in a good way. The email and number are from my experience never used, which makes both ways to contact them pointless. But another thing is is the biometric identification bot, is an obstacle to pass. I recently have been trying to access my account and it’s been a nightmare. So likewise I’ve been searching and watching online videos and reading sources on how to pass the “obstacle”. I feel like human review should be put to use more simply because it’s hard for an ai to understand something less perplexed. I think the ai  wants you to be perfect which is going to be hard for a lot of people. Currently writing this review I have not gotten fully into my account due to the 2fa which is the start of the problem, but hopefully I can get back into my account this week.  In conclusion, the app is great but there are some things that needs to be worked on and changed. For example the identification verification bot and a little more but that’s all. A tip before I finish is to get your 8 digit codes because those will be a life saver (while you have access to your account).

attributes.review:
Back in 2018, my artwork went viral. In fact, many pieces went viral. People were finally starting to see my work all over the world. I was getting jobs and gaining so much traction! And that’s because both my following AND non followers could see my work. I eventually gained 93 thousand followers, getting my artwork to industry professionals. This was literally something I could put on my artistic resume. 
But then 2020 rolls around, and IG decides it wants to be just like another video app. Reels are on full blast. You now have to pay to get your posts to be seen by anyone, even your own followers. Less than 1% of my followers and non followers were even seeing my work. 93k, and interactions were tanked. Then… each week, without any real idea why- I was losing a thousand followers. I wasn’t doing anything different, but the following was drifting away. No one could see my art. Eventually I made a new IG and tried to get everyone over to that one, and then… I could never access that other page again. I go back and check it… it’s following swindled by over 30k. But I will never be able to access it again. I tried contacting IG to no luck. I proved myself the owner to no luck. Needless to say… this affected my jobs. 
The algorithm change screwed artists. We had to search for a new home, and there’s been nothing. Everything either has no traction or it has ai. Instagram screwed a huge chunk of its base.

attributes.review:
Instagram has really gone downhill over the years, and it's hard to ignore the company's unethical practices and obsession with profit over user experience. First, the app is notorious for its data-stealing tendencies. Instagram collects vast amounts of personal information, often without clear consent or transparency. It feels like the platform is constantly tracking you, from what you like to where you go, all in an effort to sell your data to advertisers. The idea that your every move is monetized is unsettling, and there's very little control or accountability on Instagram's part.

Functionality-wise, Instagram has become a mess. The interface is cluttered, outdated, and user-unfriendly. What used to be a straightforward app is now buried under layers of ads, stories, and recommendations you didn’t ask for. The algorithm seems more focused on pushing sponsored content and irrelevant posts than showing you what you actually want to see. Every update brings more confusion and frustration, with features being broken or hidden behind confusing menus.

At this point, Instagram feels less like a fun social platform and more like a corporate machine designed to harvest data and maximize profits. The app's original charm has been overshadowed by constant ads, privacy concerns, and a lack of innovation. It's hard to recommend Instagram to anyone who values their privacy or a good user experience. There are much better alternatives out there.
attributes.title: Downhill and Outdated
